coverIntro: Van Dijk Techniek is a wholesaler in industrial parts with eight field sales reps, each covering their own region. This proposal focuses on one concrete problem: the weekly pipeline overview that Marloes now merges by hand every Friday, which is already out of date by Monday morning.
situation: Every rep keeps his own pipeline in a small Excel sheet: open quotes, expected value, expected closing date. Every Friday afternoon Marloes sends a reminder, then manually copies all eight sheets into one overarching Excel file. That takes her about four hours every week. By Monday it is already stale, because nothing is updated over the weekend and new conversations have happened by Monday morning. The result: in the Monday 9:00 management meeting she cannot answer 'where are we against target' with current figures. There is also no view of where deals get stuck; lost deals are only visible if a rep remembers to mark them, so the real win rate is not reliable. Exact Online is used only for invoicing and accounting, with no CRM functionality in use, and some reps note things down in email or on paper. The sheets live in a shared SharePoint folder. Reps vary in how disciplined they are about keeping their sheet up to date, so data quality will not be perfect at the start.
goals: Have an up-to-date pipeline overview ready every Monday morning without Marloes spending four hours merging sheets
See how much is open per stage, the expected revenue, and progress against target
Break the overview down per rep and per region, so it is visible who might need a push
Walk into the Monday 9:00 management meeting with current figures instead of 'let me check'
Keep the reps working in their own Excel sheets, without a CRM project
approach: We connect the eight reps' Excel sheets in the shared SharePoint folder to a Power BI dashboard that automatically brings the pipeline together. The reps keep filling in their own sheet exactly as they do now; nothing changes in their way of working. The sheets are read automatically from SharePoint every week, with a normalisation step so that differences in column structure and naming between reps do not cause problems. The dashboard shows open value per stage, expected revenue, progress against the 4.8 million target, and a breakdown per rep and per region. Where a sheet is incomplete or a deal has no expected closing date, the overview flags it as an open item instead of silently dropping it. The refresh runs automatically, so the overview is ready before the Monday 9:00 meeting without Marloes touching it.
scopeDeliverables: Connection to the reps' Excel sheets in the shared SharePoint folder, with automatic weekly reading
Normalisation step so that differences in column structure and naming between the eight reps' sheets are handled consistently
Power BI dashboard with open value per stage, expected revenue, and progress against the 4.8 million target
Breakdown per rep and per region
Flagging of incomplete sheets or deals without an expected closing date as open items, instead of silent omission
Automatic weekly refresh, ready before the Monday 9:00 management meeting
Short guide for Marloes on the weekly cycle so the automatic processing keeps working

phases.name: Week 1: scoping and data connection
phases.description: Set up the connection to the SharePoint folder, inventory the column structure of the eight sheets, and define the normalisation rules and the fixed format.

phases.name: Week 2-3: build dashboard
phases.description: Build the Power BI dashboard with open value per stage, expected revenue, progress against target, and the breakdown per rep and per region, including the open-item flags.

phases.name: Week 4: test and deliver
phases.description: Run one full weekly cycle with the real sheets, adjust based on feedback from Marloes, and deliver before the next Monday 9:00 management meeting.

investment: This project is scoped as one clearly defined problem - the up-to-date pipeline overview that is now merged by hand every week - at a fixed price. We will confirm the exact investment after a short scoping call in which we go through the SharePoint folder, the sheet structure and the desired breakdown together.
nextSteps: Approval of this proposal, followed by a short scoping call (about 30 minutes) with Marloes to go through the SharePoint folder, the sheet structure and the desired breakdown per rep and region. After that we start straight away in week 1.
